findings.title: report.json always reports CPU routes even when the GPU engine processed every file
findings.expected: actual_routes decode/resize/encode reflect the engine that actually processed the results
findings.actual: GPU runs record backend_counts={'nvimgcodec-auto': 24} while actual_routes claims decode='OpenCV/Pillow CPU', resize='Pillow/CPU float', encode='OpenCV CPU JPEG' because the derivation tests for the literals 'gpu'/'hybrid', which no longer appear after the Stage-8 rename
findings.reproduction: run 24x1800x1200 -> 1024px with --backend gpu and read report.json; measured: backend_counts={'nvimgcodec-auto': 24}, actual_routes.decode='OpenCV/Pillow CPU'
findings.cause: label/derivation drift introduced when the backend label was renamed to nvimgcodec-auto
findings.impact: every benchmark, report and GUI route readout mislabels the compute path; 'GPU acceleration' claims cannot be verified from the report; users cannot tell whether a CPU fallback occurred
findings.recommendation: derive routes from a single enum set on the Pipeline (e.g. {'nvimgcodec-auto','hybrid','cpu'}) and add a unit test asserting actual_routes for each engine
findings.regression_test: tests/test_observability or test_pipeline: run gpu backend on a fixture and assert report['actual_routes']['resize'] == 'CUDA separable kernel'
findings.fix: pipeline.actual_route_flags() is now the single source of truth; route strings derive from it; regression tests added in tests/test_pipeline.py
findings.verified: cpu -> CPU routes, gpu -> GPU routes, hybrid -> CPU decode + GPU resize/encode

findings.title: Stale .batchresize.lock in the output folder blocked every later run
findings.expected: a lock left by a crashed/killed run is detected as stale and cleared, or an actionable recovery path is offered
findings.actual: exit code 2 and 'error: [Errno 17] File exists: ...\.batchresize.lock'; the stored PID is never checked for liveness; no flag exists to clear the lock; the message gives no instruction
findings.reproduction: mdkir out; echo 1234 > out/.batchresize.lock; batchresize -i src -o out --size thumb_256 --backend cpu
findings.impact: any abnormal termination (crash, kill, Ctrl+C during a native call, or the OS) permanently blocks the output folder; observed repeatedly during this audit
findings.recommendation: check os.kill(pid, 0)/process liveness before refusing, age-based stale takeover, and a --unlock flag; message must name the file and the fix
findings.fix: safety.ResumeState.acquire() now writes a PID + process-start token, and lock_is_live() decides liveness from the token plus GetExitCodeProcess (OpenProcess alone succeeds for exited processes). A stale lock is taken over automatically; a live lock is still refused with an actionable message; new CLI flag --unlock removes a stale lock and never a live one
findings.verified: 10 new regression tests in tests/test_audit_regressions.py; full suite 365 tests / 7 pre-existing environment failures / 4 skips; two-process test confirms the concurrent run is refused (exit 2) and writes nothing

findings.title: RETRACTED (false positive): Mitchell kernel constant 16/3 is correct
findings.actual: the implementation satisfies three independent anchor checks: DC gain k(0)+2k(1)+2k(2) = 1.000000 exactly (the '5' variant would give 0.944 and darken every 1:1 resize by ~5.6%); the first/second segments reproduce the cubic B-spline exactly at B=1,C=0; the formulation is continuous at |x|=1 (0.05556 both sides) unlike the textbook transcription
findings.reproduction: mitchell_kernel over 0..2 and build_separable_weights at scale=1.0
findings.evidence: k(0)=0.888889, k(1)=0.055556, k(2)=0, DC=1.000000; 1:1 partition of unity True for all rows; constant-5 counter-example DC=0.944444
findings.cause: the audit relied on a remembered textbook formula (7x^3-12x^2+5)/6 whose constant term is inconsistent with the Mitchell-Netravali B/C anchors; the code uses 16/3 = 6-2B, which satisfies all anchors
findings.impact: none - no change made; tests/test_resampling.py assertions (8/9, 1/18) are correct
findings.recommendation: keep the implementation and the existing tests unchanged
findings.regression_test: assert k(0)+2k(1)+2k(2) == 1.0 (DC gain) - add as an explicit guard
findings.fix: no change; DC-gain guard test added (tests/test_resampling.py::test_mitchell_dc_gain_is_one)

findings.title: Preview worker tests fail in the full suite but pass in isolation (sandbox kills the worker process)
findings.expected: preview worker protocol survives for the whole suite
findings.actual: 'AssertionError: preview worker closed its protocol stream' for all 6 tests when the accumulated delete count in the audit sandbox crosses its guard threshold; the same 6 tests pass standalone
findings.reproduction: pytest tests/test_observability.py tests/test_preview.py -q (fails) vs pytest tests/test_preview.py -q (passes)
findings.evidence: safe-delete guard message with exit 3221225477 accompanies exactly these failures
findings.cause: the sandbox kills processes performing bulk file deletions; the worker deletes several temp files per request
findings.impact: CI signal is polluted; on a normal Windows run this is not expected to reproduce, but the worker's per-request temp churn is a real robustness smell
findings.recommendation: make the worker reuse a small fixed-size display buffer and unlink old files only at shutdown; mark the test as environment-sensitive
findings.regression_test: run the preview suite twice in a row without other test files

findings.title: IR-01 output-symlink guard cannot be exercised because this sandbox silently swallows symlink creation
findings.expected: test_IR01_output_links_rejected passes when symlinks are available
findings.actual: symlink_to() returns without error but Path.is_symlink() is False; the guard logic itself was verified by monkeypatching is_symlink and it raises correctly
findings.reproduction: create a directory symlink in a temp dir; check os.lstat -> 'file not found' although no error was raised
findings.cause: sandbox filesystem filter swallows reparse-point creation
findings.impact: link protection is unverifiable in this environment; verify on a normal Windows machine or in CI
findings.recommendation: keep the guard; make the test skip with a clear reason when symlink creation does not take effect
findings.regression_test: assert Path.is_symlink on a freshly created link before running the guard test

findings.title: Performance claims in README/REPORT.md predate the current pipeline and are not reproducible
findings.expected: documented throughput matches the code at HEAD
findings.actual: current HEAD measures 12.0 files/s (CPU) and 14.3 files/s (GPU) on 24x1800x1200 -> 1024px, i.e. 1.19x, not the documented 1.8-2.2x at 46-62 files/s
findings.reproduction: 24 x 1800x1200 synthetic JPEGs, 1024 contain, workers=8, batch=8, 4 passes, best of last 3
findings.cause: the prototype-era measurements were kept after the pipeline was redesigned (variants, resume, budgets, RGB path)
findings.impact: users may expect a speedup the current build does not deliver
findings.recommendation: replace the tables with the measured numbers or re-measure on the user's real photo collection before claiming any factor
findings.fix: REPORT.md now carries a re-measured section (CPU 12.0, GPU 14.3 files/s, 1.19x) and labels the old tables as historical

findings.title: Quality preset aliases are duplicated and partially undocumented
findings.expected: aliases differ or are clearly documented as aliases
findings.actual: high=light=90, balanced=medium=80, compact=strong=65; --help documents only light/medium/strong/extreme while the schema also contains maximum=95 and small=60
findings.recommendation: emit the full alias table in --help and mark duplicates
findings.fix: --quality help lists every preset with aliases (high=light, balanced=medium, compact=strong, maximum, small)

findings.title: With --skip-existing and a changed configuration the outputs are neither processed nor skipped
findings.expected: either regenerate the outputs or explain that --overwrite is required
findings.actual: measured processed=0, skipped=0 for a changed quality with --skip-existing; the code path raises FileExistsError('... use --overwrite') per output, i.e. they are reported as failures
findings.reproduction: run twice into the same folder; second run with --skip-existing and a different --jpeg-quality
findings.evidence: run output processed=0 skipped=0 (per-failure listing not captured in this run)
findings.cause: design choice: unverified outputs are treated as errors instead of being regenerated
findings.impact: silent no-op for a common workflow; users must read the errors section to learn why
findings.recommendation: state it in --skip-existing help, or auto-regenerate when the config digest differs and only skip verified outputs
findings.regression_test: assert that a config change with --skip-existing either processes every file or fails with a documented message
findings.fix: --skip-existing help explains that unverified/changed outputs are reported as errors; the per-output error message states the same

findings.title: The CPU encoder silently ignored --optimize-huffman (the flag only worked on the GPU path)
findings.expected: the --optimize-huffman flag (also exposed as a GUI checkbox) changes the JPEG encoder settings on every backend
findings.actual: CpuEngine.encode() only passed IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY and IMWRITE_JPEG_SAMPLING_FACTOR; CpuEngine had no optimize_huffman attribute at all, and _select_engine() built the CPU engine without the option, so the flag changed nothing on the CPU backend. The GPU backend (nvJPEG) honoured it. Measured on the real 30 MP agency dataset: enabling the flag changed the output byte-for-byte (0 % effect)
findings.reproduction: batchresize -i input -o out --backend cpu --sizing percent --sizing-value 80 --jpeg-quality 95 --optimize-huffman, then compare the output bytes with the same run without the flag
findings.evidence: outputs were byte-identical with and without the flag (24330 KB in both cases, 7 files); after the fix the same run produces 23897 KB (-1.8 % on downscaled content, -22..-25 % when no resize happens)
findings.cause: the option was only plumbed into the GPU engine constructor
findings.impact: users who ticked 'Optimize Huffman' in the GUI or passed the flag on a CPU-only machine silently got files 1.8-25 % larger than expected; the misleading flag also hid the real cause of large outputs (see the sizing analysis in AUDIT_REPORT_CURRENT.md)
findings.recommendation: keep the flag honoured on every backend and keep the regression test that asserts the CPU encoder honours it
findings.fix: CpuEngine now takes optimize_huffman and adds IMWRITE_JPEG_OPTIMIZE when it is set; the option is plumbed through _select_engine(), the pipeline's CPU engine creation, the CPU fallback path and the benchmark engine list. CpuEngine.encode changed from a staticmethod to an instance method (the only static call site, env.py, was updated). The output stays a baseline JPEG (verified: SOF0).
